concept_options.title: Guess, number, nudge
concept_options.hook: It does not memorize. It guesses, then turns the miss into a number.
concept_options.visual_approach: One indigo network that pulses forward, then walks error back while weights thicken.
concept_options.target_audience: Curious general YouTube viewers, first-year CS
key_points: Loss is a number with a direction.
Backprop walks that number backward so every knob can move a little.
concept_options.core_message: Learning is repeated, tiny, numbered nudges — not understanding.
concept_options.cta: Watch the loop once more: forward, loss, back, update.
concept_options.why_this_works: Fills the 60s gap left by hour-long calculus lessons and saturated brain metaphors.

concept_options.title: Loss is a compass
concept_options.hook: The network never hears 'wrong.' It only gets a number with a direction.
concept_options.visual_approach: A compass needle on a loss surface; skip the network diagram.
key_points: No verbal feedback exists inside training.
concept_options.core_message: Training is navigation on a number, not a conversation.
concept_options.cta: Next time you hear 'the model learned,' picture a compass.
concept_options.why_this_works: Hits the most common misconception, but skips showing the network itself.

concept_options.title: Chain-rule walk
concept_options.hook: Error does not jump. It walks back, gate by gate.
concept_options.visual_approach: A single path highlighted through four gates.
concept_options.core_message: The chain rule is a walk, not a jump.
concept_options.why_this_works: True to CS231n, but too much notation for a first 60 seconds.

selected_concept.rationale: User asked for a 60-second animated explainer. C1 is the only option that shows the full training loop in motion without requiring calculus on screen. Cloud production request treated as full-run authorization.

tools.why_this_provider: Only motion path available on this machine

stages.approach: One continuous 3-layer network; phase the animation to the script.

tools.why_this_provider: Remotion and HyperFrames are not installed

stages.approach: Pipe raw frames to ffmpeg, burn ASS, mix procedural bed, loudnorm.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Remotion springs + Piper VO vs ffmpeg animation + captions-as-voice
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Proceed with ffmpeg; say so on screen via captions.
quality_tradeoffs.quality_impact: No spoken VO; motion is real (weights and pulses change every frame).

alternative_paths.description: Remotion atelier + ElevenLabs when keys and Node modules exist
alternative_paths.what_changes: Spoken VO, spring typography, HyperFrames or Remotion runtime.

alternative_paths.description: This Cloud VM path: numpy + ffmpeg + ASS
alternative_paths.what_changes: Captions are the voice; procedural bed.

production_plan.art_direction: Indigo night #0B1020, lime #C8F542, paper #F4F1EA, violet pulses, coral loss. One network stays on screen the whole minute. No brain metaphor. No Netflix red, no cyan lab, no cream/brass leftover looks.

taste_profile.design_read: Calm chalkboard teacher: one diagram, changing state, lime captions.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: One background, two accents (lime / coral), paper type.
taste_profile.layout_variation: Network center, caption band, one title word at a time.
quality_gates: A muted viewer can still read the loop: forward, loss, back, update.

voice_selection.rationale: Piper and cloud TTS are unavailable on this VM.
voice_selection.delivery_style: short slam captions; script is the voice
voice_selection.pacing_policy: One phrase per 2-4 seconds; hook on frame 1.

approval.user_notes: User production request: Make a 60-second animated explainer about how neural networks learn. Recorded as full-run authorization on a Cloud VM where Remotion/HyperFrames/Piper are unavailable; ffmpeg locked.
